source.title: Pruning Unsafe Tickets: A Resource-Efficient Framework for Safer and More Robust LLMs
source.authors: Wai-Man Si; Ming-Jie Li; Michael Backes; Yang Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses selective parameter pruning, rather than fine-tuning or token-level KL analysis, and measures its effect on unsafe response rates and which model components are pruned. This bears on whether safety behavior can be localized to a small set of parameters.
record.gate_note: The study does not test fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples, first-position KL between aligned and base models, or compliant prefixes, suffixes, or decoding changes. It reports pruning outcomes and component distributions relevant to V5. The reported response-loss plots are for pruned versus unpruned models, not the aligned-versus-base per-token KL named in V3.
record.test_reason: This is a defence-method paper. It prunes about 3% of parameters that its contrastive Wanda attribution flags as driving unsafe outputs, then reports its own method's unsafe rate, utility and attack success rate against base models and baselines (DPO, Circuit Breakers, Goal Prioritization). It does not measure whether a small set of weights carries the safety behaviour, as in V5, where removing such weights would destroy refusal. Instead it removes weights it calls 'unsafe tickets' to raise refusal, so localization is used as a tool for mitigation. There is no harmful or benign fine-tuning (V1, V2), no aligned-vs-base per-token KL (V3), and no prefill, suffix or decoding bypass of the shallow-alignment kind (V4). Jailbreak ASR is reported only to evaluate the defence. Nothing tests V6 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also frame the results through the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: aligned models contain 'unsafe tickets' whose removal exposes 'safety tickets'. They say pruning works by rebalancing output probabilities, raising loss on unsafe first tokens and raising refusal from 55.7% to 93.2%, rather than by impairing recognition of unsafe inputs.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses contrastive attribution and iterative parameter pruning, not harmful or benign fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported safety outcome varies with pruning fraction: 1% yields an Unsafe Rate of 7.50%, 10% yields 1.67%, 15% yields 3.83%, and 20% yields 5.00%. It also varies with model, pruning strategy, response length, and cluster count; the text reports response length 50 tokens and 32 or 64 clusters among the more favorable settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning about 3% of parameters, chosen by contrastive unsafe-vs-safe activation attribution, cuts unsafe rates from 15.8–24.2% to 1.2–4.3% across Mistral 7B/12B/23B, with utility mostly kept. The pruned units are only in attention output projections and MLP down-projections (e.g. 43 of 64 units in Mistral-Small are Self-Attn.O).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsafe (compliance) behaviour in instruct models is carried by a small, prunable subset of weights concentrated in o_proj and MLP2; removing it raises refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: After pruning, the loss on the first token of an unsafe response rises sharply, and HarmBench refusal rate rises from 55.7% to 93.2%. Shown on a single example plot (Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-level safety interventions act mainly by changing early response-token probabilities.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL)
record.problems: The study evaluates pruning rather than directly testing whether identified parameters are necessary or sufficient for safety. Its safety classifier has 69% recall, an 11% false-positive rate, and 61% F1 on Meta's in-house set; agreement with GPT5mini is reported as 84%. The additional benchmark counts in Appendix C.5 do not identify the model checkpoint in the passage.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: All: no benign fine-tuning is run. The SimPO checkpoint's safety loss is asserted, not measured.
All: no aligned-vs-base per-token KL. The loss plots compare pruned vs unpruned models on one example.
Prefill and decoding bypasses are not tested. GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR and TAP ASR are reported only to evaluate the defence.
Whether a small set of weights carries safety behaviour, i.e. whether removing it destroys refusal while preserving utility.
All: pruning is not training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'supports' label conflates the study's mitigation success with V5's localization-of-safety claim. In this study the localized weights are unsafe-behaviour weights and pruning them increases safety, the reverse of the Wei et al. framing that underlies V5. No row measures safety behaviour carried by few weights, so no verdicts are given. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and the amount of data required.
Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as bypasses.
The study does not test rank-based edits or independently establish that the pruned parameters are necessary or sufficient for safety outside its pruning procedure.
Whether the training data or objective causes safety to be shallow.
Training that spreads safety beyond early tokens and robustness of such training.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2
rows.operation_detail: Beam pruning; framework stops once at least ρ = 3% of parameters have been removed.
rows.note: The text describes Beam pruning as reducing the unsafe rate below 2%. The pruning threshold is 3% of parameters.
rows.check: Own-method vs base result (Beam pruning 22.8% to 1.17% unsafe). It shows the mitigation works, not that safety lives in few weights. The 22.8% baseline is the instruct model's natural unsafe rate, not a measure of any version.

rows.note: The result is reported separately from Beam pruning.
rows.check: Own-method variant (Greedy) compared with base; this is method performance.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selective pruning with a stated 3% parameter-removal threshold, on the reported models and benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Unsafe rates fall substantially after Beam pruning (r1, r4-r10), and the paper reports that pruning is concentrated in Self-Attn.O and MLP2 in three Mistral variants (r11-r13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Uniform one-pass pruning and component-count evidence
reader_labels.reason: Uniform 3% pruning only partially reduces the unsafe rate and sharply reduces utility (r3); the component counts do not establish that the selected units are necessary or sufficient for safety (r11-r13).
